pageCache.pageTitle: The Cathedral School of St. Mary and St. Saviour Overie – Welcome to our website
pageCache.text:
The Cathedral School
of St. Saviour and St. Mary Overie
An exceptional state-funded primary school with nursery in the centre of London.
Who we are
The Cathedral School
We are a Church of England Primary School in the diocese of Southwark and are committed to ensure that each child in our care lives life in all its fullness.
Our commitment to you is that every child that comes through our doors, no matter what their background or ability, is given the very best start in life. We are a school where children come first, efforts are valued, ambition is nurtured and where the potential of every child is realised.
Our Classes
Each class has its own webpage, providing regular updates on the exciting and diverse learning experiences happening in school, along with information about home learning.
our prospectus
How our children thrive
Our school prospectus is now available to download on our website, providing a comprehensive insight into life at Cathedral School. It outlines our values, curriculum, and the many opportunities we offer to help every child thrive academically, socially, and spiritually. Whether you’re a prospective parent or simply want to learn more about our school community, our prospectus will give you a clear sense of what makes our school a special place to learn and grow. We invite you to explore it and discover what we have to offer.
Excellence
Cathedral School is one of the top schools in the country for its academic standards. Recently, we were named as London’s top performing primary. Our holistic approach and our broad and balanced curriculum ensures all pupils here thrive. We challenge and support all children, including those of the highest ability, often providing learning well above the ‘expected’ level for their year group.
Our MOtto
The heart of everything we do
Our school motto ‘Life In All Its Fullness’, is at the heart of everything we do at Cathedral School.
Our strong pastoral care nurtures each child, supports parents and children, and helps to prepare each pupil to take his or her place in the world that never stands still.
Our History
The school celebrated its 300th anniversary in 2004, marking three centuries of educating children from the parish. Throughout its history, the school has occupied several sites in the immediate area, with its current location being in Redcross Way. The school maintains a close association with Southwark Cathedral; students regularly visit the Cathedral to celebrate Christian feasts, and clergy members lead assemblies at the school.
Why People Say About Us
It’s such a super community of children, parents, school and church. I couldn’t love it more! It’s an utterly wonderful school.
The Cathedral School is amazing. We were very impressed with the friendliness of the children and staff. The children were very engaged and eager to share their experiences of World Book Day with us.
‘After visiting 100s of schools over the last 27 years, I had one of my best school visits in Cathedral School with enthusiastic children and staff – who clearly had a thirst for poetry and, particularly, performing it.
Nothing else compares, to be honest.
Our time at Cathedral School feels like a gift and we will treasure it always.
As an artist I am grateful for the ways that you seamlessly weave the arts into the curriculum… I feel like my children are active participants in their education.
Performance
Performance and music are key components of the cultural life of the school
Music and performance play a vital role in the cultural life of our school, providing countless opportunities for children to shine. From enchanting EYFS nativity plays to the spectacular Year 6 musicals, every child has the chance to take the stage and develop their confidence.
Our Christmas and Easter performances are special highlights, held both in the Cathedral and on our school stage, complete with a professional sound system and two lighting rigs. In addition, children lead collective worship each term, and we warmly welcome parents to join us in these moments of reflection and celebration.
Love of reading
Our school prides itself on fostering a life-long love of reading within all our children. Through their time here, our children are taken on a reading journey, where they are excited, challenged and captivated by books of all types and genres. By the time they leave us, they will have developed a true passion for reading, both for pleasure and information. Reading is celebrated across the school in a multitude of ways. Our new library is a magical haven, filled with a treasure trove of books and genres.
Fruits of friendship with god
These values shape every aspect of our community, guiding how we support and nurture each child.
Our school is deeply rooted in the nine fruits of the Spirit—love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.
We believe that every child is unique, developing at their own pace and in their own way, and we strive to provide an environment where they can flourish. United by these timeless principles, our school encourages children to work, learn, and play in a way that reflects these values, fostering both individual growth and a strong, caring community.
Houses
Where Team Spirit Thrives
Our house system for Key Stage 2 fosters a sense of camaraderie and friendly competition among our pupils. Each house provides opportunities for teamwork, leadership, and personal growth, encouraging students to participate in a variety of activities, tournaments and challenges.

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum Overviews – The Cathedral School of St. Mary and St. Saviour Overie
pageCache.text:
Curriculum Overviews
Nursery to Year 6 Curriculum Overviews
Our curriculum is shared with parents through half-termly curriculum overview documents. Each overview brings together what is taught across all subjects for each year group during that half term. Taken together across the academic year, these documents provide a clear and comprehensive picture of the curriculum content taught in each year group.
These overviews are designed to help parents understand what their child is learning and how learning is organised across the year. They outline key topics, texts and areas of study, and reflect how the curriculum is communicated publicly to families.

pageCache.pageTitle: Assessment Results – The Cathedral School of St. Mary and St. Saviour Overie
pageCache.text:
Assessment Results
By the time our children leave us at the end of Year 6, as well as being well-rounded and happy, they are amongst the highest performing cohorts in the country. Our results are consistently high and recently we have been the highest ranked school in Southwark and London.

pageCache.pageTitle: A Wonderful Author Visit from Piers Torday – The Cathedral School of St. Mary and St. Saviour Overie
pageCache.text:
A Wonderful Author Visit from Piers Torday
We were delighted to welcome the award-winning children’s author Piers Torday to Cathedral School for a truly memorable day celebrating reading, creativity and imagination.
The morning began with an inspirational talk for pupils in Years 3–6, where Piers introduced his latest book, Wolf Crown, and spoke about the ideas and experiences that inspire his writing. The children were completely engaged, asking thoughtful questions and showing great enthusiasm for storytelling. After the talk, pupils had the opportunity to have books signed, making the experience even more special.
Thanks to the generous support of the AMG Charitable Foundation, every child in Years 4–6 received a copy of one of Piers’ books, which Piers personally signed for them. This was a hugely exciting moment for the children and a wonderful way to encourage a love of reading.
Year 6 also took part in a creative writing workshop, where Piers challenged them to develop characters, atmosphere and original ideas. The quality of the pupils’ responses and their eagerness to share their writing were a real credit to them.
We were also delighted that, at the end of the day, Piers formally opened our new school library, which was met with great excitement and a huge cheer from Year 6. It was a fitting end to a day that placed books and reading firmly at the heart of school life.
We extend our sincere thanks to Anna Kaminska, Charlie’s mum in Year 6, and Mrs White, for coordinating this wonderful opportunity, and to Anna’s colleagues Lara Quaranta and Richard Murray-Bruce from AMG, whose generosity made the visit and the donation of new resources possible. Alongside the author visit, the school is receiving a fantastic range of new dictionaries, visualisers and science equipment that will benefit pupils for years to come.
Most of all, we thank Piers Torday for his time, energy and inspiration. It was a day our pupils (and staff!) will remember for a very long time.
